_README: Stage 3 of the weather composition. Compile with
weather_oracle's `pricing` block lifts four leaves out of this
recommended_size_usd. They must exist here by those names;
THE BLOCK THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE AUDIT
`resolution_audit_agrees` is the field that can invalidate the entire
chain. If the market's verbatim text settles on a different station
than Stage 1 forecast, no amount of calibration quality rescues it —
the pipeline has priced the wrong question. It is a boolean in the
document rather than a caveat in prose precisely so weather_oracle's
Stage 4 can act on it mechanically.
title: Weather market pricing
description: Stage 3: the market's own resolution text audited against the settlement target, then the calibrated probability priced against the live order book net of fees, with a sized recommendation. The audit is retrieved and the sizing is a judgement, and the split is what lets a coordinator tell a mispriced market from a misread one.

blocks.name: resolution_audit
blocks.description: What the market's own text says it settles on, versus what was forecast.

source.response_field: the event's verbatim resolution criteria, its full outcome ladder and the CLOB token ids

blocks.why: The verbatim text, retrieved rather than remembered, because this is the block that can invalidate everything upstream. Polymarket either returns the event or it does not. `resolution_audit_agrees` is the load-bearing field and it is a boolean rather than a caveat so the coordinator can act on it mechanically: if the market settles on a station the forecast did not use, the chain priced the wrong question and the correct output is a refusal, not a discounted recommendation.

resolution_text.description: Verbatim, not paraphrased. A paraphrase of a settlement rule is a new settlement rule.

resolution_audit_agrees.description: Whether the market's stated station, day and unit match the settlement target Stage 1 forecast. FALSE INVALIDATES THE ENTIRE CHAIN. Null means the audit could not be performed, which is not the same as agreement and must not be read as such.

station_trap_flagged.description: Whether the registry cross-check found a known station trap — Polymarket NYC settling on KLGA rather than Central Park, Dallas on Love Field rather than DFW. These are the errors that look like nothing and cost everything.

blocks.name: book
blocks.description: The live order book for the outcome token.

source.response_field: normalised bids and asks, book-quality flags, fee-adjusted EV and Kelly sizing for one outcome token

blocks.why: Deferred rather than complete: the book is only fetched once a specific outcome token has been identified, so a question asked before the ladder is resolved has no book because the call has not been made. Book quality is carried alongside the prices because a wide or one-sided book makes a nominal edge unrealisable, and a mid-price quoted from an empty book is a number with no counterparty.

implied_probability.description: The market's own probability, from the book rather than from a last-traded price. Last-traded is history; the book is what you can actually transact against.

blocks.name: valuation
blocks.description: The calibrated probability priced against the book, net of fees.

source.response_field: fee-adjusted EV and Kelly sizing computed by the tool for the supplied probability

blocks.why: Sourced rather than inferred because the tool performs this arithmetic itself given a probability: the fee adjustment and the Kelly fraction are computed, not judged. Deferred for the same reason as `book` — no token, no computation. The distinction from `recommendation` below is the point of splitting them: what the arithmetic says and what this agent advises are different claims, and a coordinator should be able to see them disagree.

edge_after_fees.description: Fee-adjusted expected edge in probability points. The number Stage 4 compares against the calibration error bar: an eight-point edge on a correction with ten points of uncertainty is not an edge.

blocks.name: recommendation
blocks.description: What this agent actually advises, which may be less than the arithmetic allows.

source.from: the fee-adjusted edge in `valuation`, discounted for book quality, for the audit result in `resolution_audit`, and for the calibration error bar supplied by Stage 2

blocks.why: A judgement, and deliberately separate from `valuation` so the two can differ visibly. Kelly says one thing; a full Kelly stake on a market whose resolution audit is null, or whose book is one-sided, is not what a careful analyst would advise. Stamped `model_inference` as a constant, because a recommendation presented as a computed figure is how a sizing judgement acquires unearned authority — and this is the block that moves real money.

recommended_side.description: `none` is a first-class recommendation and the correct one whenever the audit failed, the book is unusable, or the edge does not clear the calibration uncertainty.

recommended_size_usd.description: Typically below the Kelly fraction in `valuation`. A recommendation equal to full Kelly on every market is a sign nothing is being discounted.

size_discount_reasons.description: Why the recommendation sits below what the arithmetic allowed. An empty list beside a below-Kelly size means the discount was applied without a stated reason.

blocks.name: summary
blocks.why: Prose for whoever reads the stage alone, and the highest-risk field in this document: a fluent paragraph about a market reads as a recommendation even when `recommended_side` is `none`. It must state the refusal when there is one, and must not quote an edge the valuation block does not carry.
